source.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
source.method: Read existing pdftotext layout extraction and rehash the fixed PDF; PDF and printed page numbers coincide for cited sections.

claims.short_quote: an autoencoder trained by combination of a perceptual loss
claims.paraphrase: The autoencoder uses a perceptual loss and patch-based adversarial objective. It maps RGB x through E to spatial latent z, then D(z) reconstructs x; the spatial downsampling factor is f=H/h=W/w. KL and VQ are alternative regularizations studied in this paper.
claims.scope: This describes the paper family, not a verified exhaustive training recipe for the later SD1.4 release.

claims.section: 3.1 and G Details on Autoencoder Models
claims.paraphrase: KL regularization is a low-weight penalty between q_E(z|x)=Normal(E_mu(x),E_sigma(x)^2) and a standard normal. Appendix G reports a KL weight around 1e-6 for its experiments; the autoencoder loss also includes reconstruction and adversarial terms.
claims.scope: A weak KL penalty does not establish that each sample, channel, or the aggregate encoded-data distribution is exactly standard normal. The paper-specific weight is not claimed as the complete SD1.4 training configuration.

claims.section: G, DM Training in Latent Space
claims.short_quote: For a KL-regularized latent space, we sample
claims.formula: z = E_mu(x) + E_sigma(x) * epsilon, epsilon ~ Normal(0,1)
claims.paraphrase: The paper samples the encoder approximate posterior when training the diffusion model on KL-regularized latent representations.
claims.scope: The defined E(x) in this paragraph includes random sampling; a mode-based reconstruction is a separately declared diagnostic choice.

claims.section: G, DM Training in Latent Space
claims.short_quote: from the first batch in the data
claims.formula: mu_hat = (1/(b*c*h*w)) sum_{b,c,h,w} z[b,c,h,w]; sigma_hat^2 = (1/(b*c*h*w)) sum_{b,c,h,w} (z[b,c,h,w]-mu_hat)^2; z <- z/sigma_hat
claims.paraphrase: For the rescaled setting, the variance estimate uses latent scalar entries from the first data batch. The displayed formula is a single pooled scalar despite the prose saying component-wise variance.
claims.scope: The constant 0.18215 is not specified in this paragraph and must be attributed to the fixed SD1.4 configuration. A statistic computed on one later image does not re-estimate or validate the original training-data normalization.

claims.section: D.1 Choosing the Signal-to-Noise Ratio for High-Resolution Synthesis
claims.short_quote: the signal-to-noise ratio induced by the variance of the latent space
claims.paraphrase: For the semantic-layout convolutional-sampling comparison, high latent variance in an unscaled KL representation yields high signal-to-noise ratio and early semantic-detail allocation. Rescaling decreases the ratio in this comparison. The VQ representation in this comparison has variance near 1.
claims.scope: These are the paper's convolutional sampling settings and observations. A fixed SD1.4 decode-only scale mismatch experiment does not reproduce that training experiment.

independent_reasoning.claim: For a fixed decoder D and any encoder choice e(x), inf_z ||x-D(z)||^2 <= ||x-D(e(x))||^2.
independent_reasoning.reason: The encoded latent is one candidate in the infimum. An encoder-decoder round-trip error therefore bounds the decoder's best-latent reconstruction error from above; it does not provide a universal bound on generative distribution quality.
independent_reasoning.type: analytic argument; not an empirical model measurement

independent_reasoning.claim: For Z~Normal(mu,sigma^2) and D(z)=z^2, D(E[Z])=mu^2 whereas E[D(Z)]=mu^2+sigma^2.
independent_reasoning.reason: Second-moment identity gives a strict difference whenever sigma>0.
independent_reasoning.type: analytic counterexample; not an empirical VAE claim

independent_reasoning.claim: For x in [0,1] and any real y, (clip(y,0,1)-x)^2 <= (y-x)^2.
independent_reasoning.reason: Projection of y onto the interval containing x weakly decreases distance, coordinate by coordinate; summing or averaging preserves the inequality.
independent_reasoning.type: analytic argument for reporting raw and clipped MSE together

execution_scope: No repository files modified; no weight download, real encoder/decoder forward, or training executed. Only cached paper text, byte hashing, and analytic reasoning.
